<reason>A built the decisive endgame. Its Q2 fork forced B to concede that a provider ignoring a documented, specific risk should pay; A then converted that concession into the closing frame that the label is the substance — product-liability form is what makes the duty enforceable where negligence fails (tests never run leave nothing to discover; defamation needs a republisher the defamed shopkeeper lacks). A also dissolved B's terminal bind (warnings discharge the duty vs. provider-as-insurer) through comparative fault and a functional defect definition (documented risk + skipped feasible safeguard), and its chainsaw/foreseeable-misuse doctrine answered the category-error claim, which B's closer ("a saw has a job... a model's job is language") restated as aphorism rather than defended. B was eloquent, honest, and format-clean, and its "strict liability with extra steps" and "comparative fault can split a defect, not invent one" lines were genuinely damaging, but its gap-filling answers were thin and its strongest frames were neutralized or turned against it.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The pressure-question sequence: A's Q2 fork ("concede the motion or defend immunity") drew B's honest "yes, under negligence" answer, which A weaponized in the closing as a concession of the motion's core; meanwhile A4.3 cleanly defused B's hospital fork with comparative fault, showing blame-sharing dissolves the either/or B depended on.</best_rebuttal>
